title: India-Taiwan Action-Comedy 'Demon Hunters' Sets October 29 Netherlands Release
excerpt: Mei-Juin Chen's action-comedy — the first-ever Taiwan-India co-produced feature, starring Arjan Bajwa and JC Lin — expands its theatrical run to Dutch cinemas on October 29.
body:
• Mei-Juin Chen's India-Taiwan action-comedy Demon Hunters — the first-ever Taiwan-India co-produced feature — opens in cinemas across the Netherlands on October 29 via LAX Entertainment, according to a Variety exclusive.
  • The film stars India's Arjan Bajwa as Sanjay, an Indian tech expert and grandson of a legendary exorcist, opposite Taiwan's JC Lin as Tommy, a paranormal YouTuber who fakes exorcisms for views — alongside Regina Lei, Jack Kao and Harry Chan.
  • Its run began theatrically in Taiwan (December 31, 2025) and continued on streaming and digital platforms in India and the U.S.; it has also premiered on JioHotstar and Amazon Prime Video in multiple languages including Hindi, Tamil, Telugu, Mandarin and English.
  • Where to watch: Dutch readers can look for listings at Pathé and other leading Dutch cinemas from October 29; readers in India and the U.S. can find it on streaming and digital platforms. Watch the official trailer on YouTube.

The Netherlands is getting its first taste of the first-ever Taiwan-India co-produced feature film. Demon Hunters, Mei-Juin Chen's action-comedy blending Taiwanese mythology with Indian storytelling, will open in cinemas across the Netherlands on October 29 via LAX Entertainment, Variety reported in an exclusive.

LAX Entertainment chief Soeniel Sewnarain has lined up screens with leading Dutch exhibitors, among them Pathé — extending a run that began theatrically in Taiwan and continued on streaming and digital platforms in India and the U.S., according to the Variety report.

What came before: a historic co-production

Demon Hunters is a genuinely new cinematic pairing: produced by Light House Productions (Taiwan) and Kleos Entertainment Group (India), with producers Cindy Shyu and Gayathiri Guliani, it is the first feature ever co-produced between the two industries. The film was featured at the 2024 Cannes Film Market ahead of its global rollout, filmed in Taiwan in October 2023, and opened theatrically in Taiwan on December 31, 2025. It reached digital and VOD on August 7, and premiered on JioHotstar and Amazon Prime Video in Hindi, Tamil, Telugu, Mandarin and English — reflecting its multilingual DNA: the film is made in Taiwanese Mandarin, Hindi, English and Cantonese.

Technically, it is ambitious: the production mounted more than 700 VFX shots, drew on internationally acclaimed crew members, and fused the two industries' musical traditions into a unified soundtrack — including a Bollywood-style number, "Dadaji Ka Jadoo," distributed by Sony Music Taiwan. Cinematography came from Hong Kong veteran Tony Cheung.

Who's in it

The film stars India's Arjan Bajwa as Sanjay — an Indian tech expert and grandson of a legendary exorcist — and Taiwan's JC Lin as Tommy, a YouTuber who fakes exorcisms for views until he encounters a real supernatural entity. The supporting cast includes Regina Lei as Arumi, veteran Jack Kao, and Harry Chan. Screenplay is by Po-Jung Hua and Jun-You Wu, with Yong Yu Huang and Chen-Shing Yeh producing.

"This is a great step toward building globally resonant IP from Asia. It demonstrates how culturally rooted stories can transcend borders and unlock new film audience ecosystems."

— Gayathiri Guliani, producer, Kleos Entertainment Group

Why this matters for the diaspora

For Indian audiences, the film is a new kind of crossover: not an Indian film released abroad, but a genuinely shared production — an Indian lead, Indian storytelling DNA and Hindi music elements woven into a Taiwanese genre machine. Director Mei-Juin Chen has noted she is proud that three women filmmakers from different cultures came together to tell a story traditionally told from a male perspective.

For diaspora readers in the Netherlands, the theatrical release is the immediate hook: check Pathé and other major Dutch exhibitors from October 29. For readers in the U.S. and India, the film is already on streaming and digital platforms — streaming on JioHotstar and Prime Video in multiple Indian languages plus Mandarin and English.

What to watch

The Netherlands theatrical run is the next data point in an experiment: can a cross-border genre film build sustained international demand? LAX Entertainment's push into Dutch screens — and the film's reception there — will signal whether Taiwan-India co-productions have a repeatable theatrical path beyond festivals. If it works, more such collaborations are likely to follow: the producers have said their hope is "to do even more cross-cultural and cross-country collaborations."
